Bill.BriefDescription: Concerning the restoration of the right to vote for people who were convicted of felonies.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to the restoration of the right to vote for peoplewho were convicted of felonies; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Under law there is no clear way to determinewhen voting rights are restored to a person who has been convicted ofa felony. This creates confusion and unnecessary barriers to voting.It also discriminates against certain groups of citizens. For example,approximately seventeen percent of AfricanAmericans and ten percent ofLatinos are prevented from voting. It is the intent of the legislatureto create a clear delineation to determine when a person convicted ofa felony, upon meeting specific responsibilities of his or hersentence, becomes eligible to gain the restoration of the right tovote. The office of the secretary of state is directed to review currentstatutes and regulations as they relate to the restoration of felon'sright to vote and recommend a solution to the 2010 legislature.
